construct: X-linked sideroblastic anemia is caused by pathogenic variants in ALAS2, the erythroid-specific mitochondrial 5-aminolevulinate synthase that catalyzes the first and rate-limiting step of heme synthesis. Impaired heme production causes ineffective erythropoiesis and mitochondrial iron accumulation, producing ring sideroblasts; iron stores are normal or increased rather than depleted. ALAS2 requires pyridoxal 5'-phosphate, explaining the variable pyridoxine responsiveness of many cases.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: An adolescent male with an affected maternal uncle, microcytosis, increased iron indices, normal blood lead, and marrow ring sideroblasts has an X-linked inherited heme-synthesis defect, classically ALAS2-related sideroblastic anemia.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Lead poisoning can produce microcytic sideroblastic changes, but the blood lead is normal and the maternal-male pedigree supports a heritable X-linked process. Beta-thalassemia can be microcytic with normal/high iron but does not characteristically produce ring sideroblasts.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The iron-loading ring-sideroblast phenotype plus X-linked pedigree and normal lead level make ALAS2-related X-linked sideroblastic anemia uniquely best.
